scope: Modelling methods and representation only. All component dimensions, configuration choices and mounting coordinates must be supplied by the consolidated design specification and spatial architect.
recommended_pipeline: One canonical, versioned parameter and evidence registry owned by the main agent
A spatial contract with immutable axis conventions, named anchors and locked shared dimensions
Separate component JSON documents conforming to one strict JSON Schema
Python wrapper validates JSON and semantic assembly constraints before launching Blender
Pinned local Blender executes a deterministic, allowlisted operation interpreter
Editable component objects, curves and modifiers are saved in one .blend
Orthographic geometry views and matched perspective reference views are rendered separately
Independent visual review ranks major shape and proportion errors before cosmetic details
Central parameter changes and component revisions produce a fresh build and validation report

environment.verification_method: Read-only shell commands and headless factory-startup API introspection
notes: Use uv for the external Python wrapper, validation and report generation; Blender scripts use Blender's bundled Python.
A Python 3.14 wrapper must not assume its packages or interpreter are available inside Blender.
No Blender MCP connection, remote generation service or OpenAI API integration is necessary.

shared_json_recommendation.unknown_properties: Reject through additionalProperties:false on all structured objects
shared_json_recommendation.numeric_convention: Millimetres and degrees in JSON; convert once in renderer or consistently use millimetre-scaled Blender units

alternatives: object with required param:string, optional scale:number default 1 and offset:number default 0
scalar.reference_semantics: Resolve named canonical value, then multiply by scale and add offset. Units are inherited; scale is dimensionless.
restrictions: No free-form expressions, eval, Python source, imports, shell commands or arbitrary file paths in component JSON
Precompute nontrivial derived dimensions centrally and record their derivation
Unknown references, nonfinite results and unresolved cycles are hard errors
Literal values in shared dimensions are rejected by semantic validation; use parameter references

registry_parameter_fields.confidence_basis: short text distinguishing numeric confidence from evidence strength
registry_parameter_fields.uncertainty: optional stated tolerance or estimate interval, with method; never invent manufacturer tolerance
registry_parameter_fields.derivation: optional description and referenced input IDs
registry_parameter_fields.locked: boolean; component agents cannot override locked parameters

evidence_source_fields.url: original primary source or manufacturer asset URL
evidence_source_fields.title: source title
evidence_source_fields.kind: manufacturer_text | dimensioned_drawing | photograph | mesh_reference | local_runtime | method_documentation
evidence_source_fields.variant: exact product revision/configuration depicted, or unresolved
evidence_source_fields.asset_sha256: optional hash of a locally obtained reference
evidence_source_fields.locator: section, image label, screenshot crop or drawing callout

component_document_fields.contract_sha256: hash of immutable contract used by the component author
component_document_fields.nodes: ordered geometry operations with unique local IDs
component_document_fields.anchors: named local feature points; main architecture establishes assembly placements
component_document_fields.validation: component checks referring to canonical limits

geometry_node_fields.id: stable name, used for Blender object and report identity
geometry_node_fields.transform: location vector, rotation_deg XYZ vector and positive scale vector with documented application order
geometry_node_fields.modifiers: optional ordered allowlist such as bevel, solidify, subdivision, mirror

assembly_fields.coordinates: fixed handedness, up axis, forward axis and origin
assembly_fields.component_files: manifest of component IDs and relative JSON paths
assembly_fields.instances: component reference, stable instance ID, parent anchor and transform
assembly_fields.materials: named Principled shader settings; estimated optical values labelled
assembly_fields.views: named camera positions/targets, projection type, orthographic scale or focal length, resolution and role
assembly_fields.checks: geometric, dimensional, evidence and coverage checks
assembly_fields.build: Blender version, seed, renderer settings, source hashes and quality tier

geometry_operations.use: PCB substrate, chips, connector blocks and simple battery envelope
geometry_operations.caution: Box sizes must be modelled in mesh coordinates before dimensional bevel/solidify operations, rather than retained as nonuniform object scale.

geometry_operations.use: Motor can, shaft, camera barrel, screw shank
geometry_operations.caution: Use coaxial ring or radial profile meshes for bores instead of pretending a solid cylinder is hollow.

geometry_operations.use: Thin propeller ducts, motor bearing rings and camera mount ring
geometry_operations.implementation: Explicit inner/outer loops and bridged top/bottom quads; fixed angular sample ordering.
geometry_operations.extension: A radial-z cross-section revolved about the duct axis supports taper, moulded lips and varying wall profile without booleans.

geometry_operations.use: Wires, antenna lead and rounded thin struts
geometry_operations.implementation: Editable Curve data with bevel for round wire, or deterministic transported frames for explicit nonround strut profiles.
geometry_operations.caution: Straight cylindrical bars are only a prototype representation when reference struts have tapered or rectangular moulded sections.

geometry_operations.use: PCB outline, flat braces, mounting tabs and strap loops
geometry_operations.implementation: Consistent winding; deterministic planar triangulation for caps; bridge side loops.
geometry_operations.caution: Concave outlines and holes require actual triangulation or constrained topology, never a single nonplanar n-gon.

geometry_operations.use: Hollow curved canopy and nonuniform moulded shapes
geometry_operations.implementation: Section positions and corresponding 2D profile samples define predictable quad topology; preserve intended open underside and apertures. An editable Solidify modifier can add thickness.
geometry_operations.caution: Equal vertex count/winding across profile sections is mandatory. Solidify thickness is an approximation on curved topology; measure evaluated geometry where exact thickness matters.

geometry_operations.use: Parametric propeller planform and pitch twist
geometry_operations.implementation: Each spanwise station defines radius, chord, sweep, vertical offset, twist and thickness; construct top/bottom foil surfaces with a closed tip. Instance one blade radially by the centrally specified blade count.
geometry_operations.caution: Propeller diameter, pitch and blade count are supplied by the Air65 II configuration contract. A photographed silhouette cannot verify its airfoil or exact pitch distribution.

geometry_operations.use: Compact escape hatch for explicit original topology under the same structured-data contract
geometry_operations.implementation: Mesh.from_pydata, mesh validation, deterministic vertex and face order.
geometry_operations.caution: Require provenance and sensible size limits. Raw mesh input must not bypass dimensional or shared-anchor checks.

editing_policy: Give every component its own Blender collection and parent Empty; stable instance names prevent ambiguity.
Keep wires as editable curves and retain useful bevel/solidify/subdivision modifiers.
Keep cutters in a hidden named collection if any boolean apertures are needed; use robust solver and inspect evaluated output.
Preserve original JSON and build metadata in Blender Text datablocks or custom properties so edits can be traced.
Be explicit that JSON changes regenerate geometry; manual .blend edits are editable but are not automatically written back to JSON.
determinism_policy: Run from factory startup with a documented Blender binary and --python-exit-code 1.
Use bpy.data and direct mesh creation rather than UI-state-dependent operators; use operators only for supported save/render steps.
Sort files and IDs, use fixed tessellation and sampling counts, fixed camera transforms and no random geometry.
Specify render engine, CPU or device, resolution, samples, random seed, world, light placement, color management and transparency.
Record canonical JSON hashes, Blender build hash, resolved parameters, object bounds and mesh statistics.
Compare semantic scene and rounded mesh-coordinate hashes for regeneration, rather than assuming byte-identical .blend files.
Exact pixels across different Blender builds or GPU devices are not guaranteed; limit a determinism claim to the tested build/device/settings.

pre_blender: JSON Schema validation for every document and operation
No duplicate IDs, missing materials, unresolved parameters or stale contract hashes
No shared dimension overrides by component documents
Positive wall thickness, valid segment counts, consistent loft samples and face indices
post_geometry: Motor/duct/prop coaxiality and central architecture anchor agreement
Wheelbase and outer envelope derived from evaluated geometry
Prop swept radius versus duct inner radius and vertical clearance
PCB mounting holes, fastener axes and standoffs align
Camera optical axis equals contracted tilt and faces forward
Boundary/nonmanifold edges reported with explicit acceptable exceptions
Bounding boxes and nominal evaluated dimensions compared with declared tolerances
visual: Top, bottom, front, rear, left, right and three-quarter views
Neutral clay or silhouette views for geometry, separate material beauty render
Reference photo camera alignment before judging proportions
Landmark pixel deltas and silhouette overlap only when view and projection are matched
Reviewer ranks frame layout, duct-to-body proportion, canopy silhouette, camera placement, motor height, blade form, then colors/details
Mark unseen geometry, uncertain optical properties and estimated dimensions in final report

open_source_options.name: Blender Python API
open_source_options.decision: Recommended core runtime; already installed and verified locally.
open_source_options.reason: Direct editable mesh/curve creation, materials, cameras, modifiers and headless rendering without extra add-ons.

open_source_options.name: Sverchok
open_source_options.decision: Relevant parametric-node reference; not needed for the initial renderer.
open_source_options.reason: Supports procedural meshes, profiles, transforms, curves and surfaces, but adds add-on/version dependencies and a larger execution surface.

open_source_options.name: build123d
open_source_options.decision: Optional future path for exact BREP and mechanical fit; not required for Blender-first visual recreation.
open_source_options.reason: Open Cascade CAD kernel offers precise solids, while tessellation/import introduces another stack and does not by itself make photographic canopy geometry accurate.

open_source_options.name: TerminalSkills blender-scripting skill
open_source_options.decision: Read as a public implementation reference only; not installed or adopted as authority.
open_source_options.reason: Covers headless invocation, direct meshes, modifiers, curves and version caveats. Verify recipes against installed Blender.

open_source_options.name: pinion05 blender-headless-skill
open_source_options.decision: Useful older headless example/test catalogue; no installation needed.
open_source_options.reason: Targets Blender 4.2, so examples must be rechecked against local Blender 5.2.2.

reference_asset_policy.policy: If an official file is later found, record its exact revision, source, hash, units and license. It can serve as an explicitly labelled measurement or comparison reference; do not silently substitute it for generated component JSON or assume its reuse license.
